newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia puts poll riot death toll at 124.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia puts poll riot death toll at 124.

text.p: Indonesian police on Wednesday put the death toll in last week's riot and arson attacks in the South Kalimantan provincial capital of Banjarmasin at 124, the official Antara news agency reported.

Local newspapers in Banjarmasin had earlier reported that up to 142 died in the violence which started on Friday afternoon with clashes between rival political supporters on the last day of Indonesia's violence-marred election campaign.
Antara quoted Indonesian national police chief Lieutenant-General Dibyo Widodo as telling reporters in Jakarta that 124 bodies had been found. Only 15 had been identified.
Banjarmasin mayor Sadjoko was quoted as saying the city administration was preparing a mass grave for the unidentified victims.

Most of the dead were killed in a fire at the Mitra Plaza shopping complex late in the evening after rioters rampaged through the centre of the riverside town of 400,000 people, destroying shopping centres, hotels, churches, banks, shops and vehicles.
Widodo said the dead at Mitra Plaza were not shop employees but looters as all employees had been sent home earlier. He did not rule out more bodies being found.

The disturbance started in the early afternoon as supporters of the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) attacked rivals from the ruling Golkar party on the final day of the election campaign.
The country has been quiet during a five-day cooling off period leading up to the national and local elections on Thursday.
